Package org.jdesktop.lg3d.apps.remoteviewer

Class ViewerHost

java.lang.Object
org.jdesktop.lg3d.apps.remoteviewer.ViewerHost
public final class ViewerHost extends Object
Hosts the Remote Viewer's live-viewing panel (Recorder.viewerPanel) inside whichever desktop is running, so the viewer window belongs to the desktop and is captured by the desktop screenshot instead of escaping it as a stray top-level OS window beside the desktop.

The old code created a ViewerGUI JFrame eagerly from Recorder's constructor. A top-level JFrame is owned by the host window manager: it is neither a child of the 2D desktop's JDesktopPane nor part of the 3D scene, so the internal screen capture painted each top-level frame into its own file and the viewer never landed in lgscreen-0-0.png. This host embeds the shared panel instead, choosing the container at runtime:

  1. 2D desktop - Desktop2D.openHostedPanel(java.lang.String, javax.swing.Icon, javax.swing.JComponent) wraps the panel in an MDI Desktop2DWindow (a JInternalFrame). Returns null when no 2D desktop is running.
  2. 3D desktop - TitledSwingWindow.show(java.lang.String, javax.swing.JPanel, int, int) hosts the panel on a SwingNode inside a Frame3D. Guarded by try/catch: with no 3D toolkit it throws and we fall through.
  3. Standalone - ViewerGUI, a plain JFrame, so the CLI Main ... viewer mode (no desktop in the JVM) still works.

Each host wires the panel's three hooks onto its own window idioms; when hosted, "full screen" means maximize-within-desktop (never exclusive OS full-screen, which the standalone JFrame handles on its own).
